about.text: Brocciu is a Corsican cheese produced from a combination of milk and whey, giving it some of the characteristics of whey cheese. It is produced from ewe's milk. It is notable as a substitute for lactose-rich Italian ricotta, as brocciu contains less lactose.

how.text: The whey is heated in a cauldron over a strong fire, stirred all the time. Milk and salt go in around 40 °C, and at about 90 °C the proteins flocculate and rise; the liquid must never touch the cauldron wall or boil. The French page gives no whey-to-milk ratio, no acid or rennet, and no times, so none are stated. (The English page's 'just below 100 °F / 93 °C' is garbled and was not used.)

steps.name: add milk and salt
steps.note: Ewe's and/or goat's milk (at most 25 % under the AOP), water (at most 15 %) and salt go in.
The proteins flocculate at about 90 °C, and the liquid is never allowed to boil.

steps.name: mould
steps.note: Skimmed into rush moulds (fattoghje, casgiaghji), or plastic moulds for sale.
Only the brocciu passu, salted on the surface, is ripened, for at least 21 days.
